candidates.title: Draft daily order-status summaries

demandEvidence.chore: Generate a daily summary of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.

ease.reason: The supplied n8n Summarize documentation supports grouping operator-supplied fields; the proposed workflow and inputs are untested, and live access is unverified.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: multi-service operators might pay for daily summaries, but the request establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic-row prototype using documented aggregation is plausible in four weeks; field mapping, workflow execution, and live connections are untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed aggregation can prepare a draft from supplied rows; a person must validate data and decide actions, and execution is untested.

evidence.reason: The post names a daily summary and three categories, but gives no workflow detail beyond that request, demand corroboration, or implementation test.

experimentPlan.output: A daily draft summary of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests from operator-supplied rows.
inputs: Synthetic rows with order status and service category
Operator-supplied field names and reporting date
experimentPlan.trigger: Proposed daily run after an operator supplies or exports the day’s order rows.
steps: Accept a small CSV or pasted table of fictional order rows.
Ask the operator to map status and service-category fields.
Group rows by status and count completed, cancelled, and pending items.
Format the counts and list rows with missing or unrecognized statuses.
Show the draft for an operator to compare with the input and approve.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed synthetic table, verify each status count against a hand-counted expected result and confirm unrecognized rows are surfaced instead of silently counted.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies the data and field mapping, checks the summary against source records, and decides what to do with exceptions; no customer or provider action is automated.
unverified: The assigned post does not establish an actual business or recurring customer demand.
No supplied source documents access to order systems or scheduled delivery.
The n8n Summarize reference documents aggregation fields, not execution of this proposed workflow.

candidates.reason: Reassessed against checker feedback: the specific daily-summary chore supports a bounded synthetic-data experiment, but corrected supported ratings average below the 6 threshold; withdrawn from posts.

candidates.title: Prepare company-specific resume forms

demandEvidence.chore: Enter resume information into forms customized for one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

ease.reason: A beginner can test a draft that maps a supplied resume to one sample form, but no implementation reference supports form filling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: career-service providers or job seekers might pay for reducing repeated form entry; the post does not establish buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare a supplied resume with a manually provided sample form; extracting varied forms remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed tool could prepare field-by-field answers, but a person must check accuracy and submit each application.

evidence.reason: The author reports filling company-specific resume forms every day for two hours; no other affected users or workflow details are given.

experimentPlan.output: A draft mapping of fields from an operator-supplied resume to one sample employer form.
experimentPlan.trigger: A user provides a resume and a new sample form that they want to prepare.
steps: Extract the listed fields from the fictional resume.
Compare them with the operator-provided form field names.
Draft answers only where the resume explicitly contains matching information.
Mark missing or ambiguous fields for the user.
Let the user compare every answer before any manual submission.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fictional resume and sample form, check that each drafted answer matches its source text and that absent fields are marked missing.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The user provides the materials, checks every answer, decides whether it belongs in an application, and submits the form manually.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports reading or filling employer forms.
The post describes one author’s experience and does not establish buyer demand or permission to process another person’s data.

candidates.reason: Concrete repeated chore, assessed as a bounded draft-only experiment; provisional mean is below 6 because supported implementation and paying-buyer evidence are absent.
